brief_summary: Side-view cross-section of an MX-style switch with the stem drawn mid-stroke. The two collision sites a silent switch intercepts are marked in the article's dusty-rose splash — top-out where the rail shoulders meet the underside of the top housing, bottom-out where the leg feet meet the bottom-housing floor — with the elastomer pads drawn on the stem at both sites. The leaf is drawn between them in plain warm-grey and labelled as reached by neither pad, setting up the silent-tactile section.
data_sources: silent-switch-damping-deep-dive.mdx § 'Two impacts, one moving part' — 'On the downstroke, the feet of the stem's legs reach the floor of the bottom housing; on the upstroke, the spring drives the stem back until the shoulders of its rails strike the underside of the top housing.'

silent-switch-damping-deep-dive.mdx § 'Two impacts, one moving part' — 'The pad goes on the stem because the stem is the one body that touches both impact surfaces: one moving part, two pads, both collisions covered.'

silent-switch-damping-deep-dive.mdx § 'Why silent tactiles are harder' — 'That snap is a third transient inside the housing, and neither pad can reach it — it occurs in the metal, between the two surfaces the pads cover.'
https://www.cherry.de/en-us/product/mx2a-silent-black — 'The stem of MX Silent switches is made of two components and contains integrated, patented noise reduction technology.'
